alex: quick follow-up from the attention-layout RFC — ran a few microbenchmarks on NHWC vs NCHW with mixed QKV layouts, and hit surprising tail latencies on long sequences.

sara: thanks for flagging. can you share the exact kernel paths you exercised? e.g., fused mha vs separate gemm+softmax?

alex: mostly fused kernels on A100, but i also ran our fallback path (planar q/k/v -> separate matmuls) to compare. interestingly, NHWC+contig-QKV gives ~8% worse p99 beyond 2048 tokens. p50 is fine.

mike: that smells like vectorization + stride misalignment. NHWC tends to drop contiguous inner dims for K/V, which defeats warp-wide loads sometimes. did you align to 128 bytes?

alex: good call — we didn't pad to 128 for that run. padded trial to 128 and p99 improved ~4% but still worse than NCHW.

toni: did you try tile size changes in the fused kernel? small tiles can avoid register spilling but increase shared mem traffic.

alex: yeah. tile=32 vs 64: 32 reduced peak occupancy but lowered p99 at long seqs. suspect register pressure on the QKV gather path.

sara: can you paste the config you used? curious about layout flags we pass from runtime -> kernel selector.
